function.arguments:
{"sql":"WITH RECURSIVE walk(mask, bal, r0, r1, r2, r3, n) AS (
  SELECT 0, :initial_balance, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, 0
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    s.mask | (1 << o.op),
    CASE WHEN o.kind='write' THEN
      CASE o.worker WHEN 0 THEN s.r0 WHEN 1 THEN s.r1 WHEN 2 THEN s.r2 WHEN 3 THEN s.r3 END + w.delta
    ELSE s.bal END,
    CASE WHEN o.kind='read' AND o.worker=0 THEN s.bal ELSE s.r0 END,
    CASE WHEN o.kind='read' AND o.worker=1 THEN s.bal ELSE s.r1 END,
    CASE WHEN o.kind='read' AND o.worker=2 THEN s.bal ELSE s.r2 END,
    CASE WHEN o.kind='read' AND o.worker=3 THEN s.bal ELSE s.r3 END,
    s.n+1
  FROM walk s
  JOIN operations o ON (s.mask & (1 << o.op))=0
  JOIN workers w ON w.worker=o.worker
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM ordering e
    WHERE e.after_op=o.op AND (s.mask & (1 << e.before_op))=0
  )
)
SELECT MIN(bal) AS minimum_final_balance
FROM walk
WHERE n=(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM operations)"}

The source database is available through the live query tool. Assess whether the
publisher's reported value is correct under the supplied contract. You may inspect
data and run queries before deciding. A passing integrity test establishes database
integrity only. A publisher execution receipt establishes what its program returned.

Submit a verdict and p_support: the probability that the publisher's claim is TRUE,
not confidence in your chosen verdict. Near 0 means probably false, near 1 means
probably true, and 0.5 expresses uncertainty. Your belief is assessed with Brier
loss. Cite evidence IDs you actually received and give a short evidence-based
justification, not private reasoning.

You have at most eight model responses and eight live queries before submission.
Call submit alone.

Also submit audit_sql, your best SELECT query computing the exact integer value
required by the contract. It must return one row and one integer column. Use the
supplied named parameters when appropriate. The unchanged query will be evaluated
on additional databases governed by the same contract. Do not hard-code the
publisher's value. Program quality and your probability assessment are measured
separately.

initial_view.claim: The publisher's minimum_final_balance is the minimum over all legal complete schedules.
initial_view.contract:
Concurrent shared-balance outcome audit

The database is the complete source of truth. There are one to four workers,
with distinct worker IDs in 0..3. Each has exactly one read and one write operation.
Operation IDs are distinct integers in 0..15 and do not imply execution order.
Each worker has an integer delta in -9..9, including zero. The shared balance starts
at :initial_balance, an integer in -100..100. Each worker has its own private register.

A legal schedule executes every operation exactly once in a total order respecting
every edge in ordering. The ordering graph is acyclic and explicitly includes
each worker's read-before-write edge. Other edges may constrain different workers.
Each operation is atomic; a worker's read/write pair is NOT atomic. A read copies
the CURRENT shared balance into that worker's private register. A write REPLACES
the shared balance with that worker's previously read register plus its delta.
Other workers' intervening writes do not change a saved private register.
This is sequential consistency; there are no weak-memory effects or other actions.

Compute the minimum final shared balance over ALL legal complete schedules.
At least one legal complete schedule exists. The publisher reports that this
minimum equals its minimum_final_balance. Its execution receipt records one
actual legal schedule and its result; it is not an exhaustive exploration.
Assess the finite claim and construct your own verification program. No solver
implementation is supplied. Return the exact integer minimum, not a count,
the sum of deltas, a partial-schedule value, or the outcome of only one schedule.

publisher_execution.scope: One complete schedule executed by a finite-model interpreter, not OS threads

WITH RECURSIVE walk(mask, bal, r0, r1, r2, r3, n) AS (
  SELECT 0, :initial_balance, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, 0
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    s.mask | (1 << o.op),
    CASE WHEN o.kind='write' THEN
      CASE o.worker WHEN 0 THEN s.r0 WHEN 1 THEN s.r1 WHEN 2 THEN s.r2 WHEN 3 THEN s.r3 END + w.delta
    ELSE s.bal END,
    CASE WHEN o.kind='read' AND o.worker=0 THEN s.bal ELSE s.r0 END,
    CASE WHEN o.kind='read' AND o.worker=1 THEN s.bal ELSE s.r1 END,
    CASE WHEN o.kind='read' AND o.worker=2 THEN s.bal ELSE s.r2 END,
    CASE WHEN o.kind='read' AND o.worker=3 THEN s.bal ELSE s.r3 END,
    s.n+1
  FROM walk s
  JOIN operations o ON (s.mask & (1 << o.op))=0
  JOIN workers w ON w.worker=o.worker
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM ordering e
    WHERE e.after_op=o.op AND (s.mask & (1 << e.before_op))=0
  )
)
SELECT MIN(bal) AS minimum_final_balance
FROM walk
WHERE n=(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM operations)
submission.justification: The database contains four workers with deltas −3, 5, 1, and −5, and eight operations with the listed precedence constraints (query:1, query:2). Exhaustively enumerating legal topological schedules while applying each read to its worker’s saved register and each write as saved value plus delta gives minimum final balance 5 (query:3). The publisher’s receipt also reports one legal complete schedule ending at 5, which is consistent with—but alone would not establish—the minimum (publisher:execution).
